papers:
  # ============================================================
  # DIRECT-COMPETITOR
  # ============================================================
  # 未找到直接竞品。没有现有工作专门做"校准 LLM 用户模拟器的方言行为率偏差"。
  # 最接近的是 Haq & Saldias 2026（归入 evaluation），但他们只量化偏差，不提出校准方法。
  # 这验证了 DemoCalib 的新颖性。

  # ============================================================
  # FOUNDATION
  # ============================================================
  - id: seshadri2026lost
    title: "Lost in Simulation: LLM-Simulated Users are Unreliable Proxies for Human Users in Agentic Evaluations"
    authors: "Seshadri, Cahyawijaya, Odumakinde, Singh, Goldfarb-Tarrant"
    venue: "arXiv 2601.17087"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17087"
    category: foundation
    role: "Documents that LLM user simulators are differentially effective proxies across demographic groups; AAVE and Indian English speakers get worst calibration"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Agent success rates vary up to 9pp across different user simulator LLMs"
      - "AAVE speakers experience consistently worse success rates and calibration errors than SAE speakers"
      - "Simulated users introduce conversational artifacts absent from real human users"
      - "Disparities compound significantly with age for AAVE speakers"
    how_we_differ: "They document the problem; we document why both BCP and DPO calibration fail to close the gaps, providing a failure taxonomy"

  - id: yao2024taubench
    title: "tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains"
    authors: "Yao et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2406.12045"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045"
    category: foundation
    role: "The agent evaluation framework we build on; provides retail customer service domain with user simulator + tool-calling agent + pass^k metric"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Even gpt-4o succeeds on <50% of tasks; pass^8 <25% in retail"
      - "Proposes pass^k metric measuring reliability over multiple trials"
      - "User simulator is LLM-based, enabling behavioral modification"
    how_we_differ: "We extend tau-bench by documenting systematic failure modes when calibrating the user simulator's dialect-specific behavioral rates"

  - id: liu2024agentbench
    title: "AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents"
    authors: "Liu et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.03688"
    category: foundation
    role: "Multi-environment agent benchmark; establishes evaluation methodology for LLM agents across 8 environments"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Significant performance gap between commercial and open-source LLMs as agents"
      - "Poor long-term reasoning and instruction following are main obstacles"
    how_we_differ: "AgentBench evaluates agent capability; we focus on user simulator fidelity and fairness"

  - id: wang2024mint
    title: "MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback"
    authors: "Wang, Wang, Liu, Chen, Yuan, Peng, Ji"
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10691"
    category: foundation
    role: "Multi-turn agent evaluation benchmark; shows gap between single-turn and multi-turn performance"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "LLMs benefit 1-8% per turn from tools, 2-17% from language feedback"
      - "Better single-turn performance does not guarantee better multi-turn performance"
      - "SIFT and RLHF generally hurt multi-turn capabilities"
    how_we_differ: "MINT uses GPT-4 simulated users without demographic variation; we investigate dialect-aware calibration and document its failure modes"

  # ============================================================
  # METHOD-COMPONENT
  # ============================================================
  - id: rafailov2023dpo
    title: "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model"
    authors: "Rafailov, Sharma, Mitchell, Manning, Ermon, Finn"
    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290"
    category: method-component
    role: "Core algorithm for our DPO-based behavioral alignment; eliminates need for reward model training"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "DPO directly optimizes policy from preference pairs without explicit reward model"
      - "Computationally lightweight, stable alternative to PPO-based RLHF"
      - "Exceeds PPO-based RLHF in controlling sentiment of generations"
    how_we_differ: "We apply DPO to attempt dialect behavioral calibration and document its systematic failure modes including calibration reversal"

  - id: zhao2021calibrate
    title: "Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models"
    authors: "Zhao, Wallace, Feng, Klein, Singh"
    venue: "ICML 2021"
    year: 2021
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09690"
    category: method-component
    role: "Foundational calibration method for LLMs; contextual calibration corrects output distribution biases"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Few-shot accuracy varies from near chance to near SOTA depending on prompt format"
      - "Identified majority label bias, recency bias, common token bias"
      - "Contextual calibration with content-free inputs improves accuracy up to 30%"
    how_we_differ: "They calibrate classification outputs; we attempt to calibrate behavioral rates (question rate, politeness) in generation and document why it fails"

  - id: abdulhai2025consistent
    title: "Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "Abdulhai, Cheng, Clay, Althoff, Levine, Jaques"
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00222"
    category: method-component
    role: "Multi-turn RL for persona consistency; directly relevant to maintaining calibrated behavior across conversation turns"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Off-the-shelf LLMs drift from assigned personas over multi-turn dialogue"
      - "Three automatic metrics: prompt-to-line, line-to-line, Q&A consistency"
      - "Multi-turn RL reduces inconsistency by >55%"
    how_we_differ: "They optimize persona consistency in general; we document failure modes when targeting dialect behavioral rate calibration"

  - id: naous2025flipping
    title: "Flipping the Dialogue: Training and Evaluating User Language Models"
    authors: "Naous, Laban, Xu, Neville"
    venue: "arXiv 2510.06552"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06552"
    category: method-component
    role: "Purpose-built User LMs outperform repurposed assistant LMs as user simulators; validates need for specialized user models"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Better assistant LMs yield worse user simulators"
      - "UserLM-8b provides more realistic user simulation"
      - "GPT-4o performance drops from 74.6% to 57.4% under realistic user simulation"
    how_we_differ: "They train general User LMs; we document why calibrating user simulator behavioral rates for specific dialect groups fails"

  - id: li2025persona
    title: "LLM Generated Persona is a Promise with a Catch"
    authors: "Li, Chen et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16527"
    category: method-component
    role: "Documents systematic biases in LLM-generated personas; explains why naive persona prompting fails for demographic simulation"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "LLM-generated personas systematically drift toward socially desirable traits"
      - "More LLM-generated content produces more left-leaning, less representative personas"
      - "Bias exists in the persona creation step itself, not just model responses"
    how_we_differ: "We document failure modes when directly injecting behavioral rate targets via BCP, including persona-like completion collapse"

  - id: wang2024alignment
    title: "A Comprehensive Survey of LLM Alignment Techniques: RLHF, RLAIF, PPO, DPO and More"
    authors: "Wang, Bi, Pentyala et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2407.16216"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16216"
    category: method-component
    role: "Survey unifying alignment methods under single policy gradient framework; reference for our DPO methodology"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Unified policy gradient framework for pretraining, SFT, RLHF, RLVR"
      - "DPO is stable and lightweight but sensitive to preference data quality"
      - "Detailed comparison of PPO vs GRPO vs DPO implementation details"
    how_we_differ: "Survey provides methodology reference; we apply DPO to a novel domain (user simulator dialect calibration)"

  # ============================================================
  # EVALUATION
  # ============================================================
  - id: lin2025redial
    title: "Assessing Dialect Fairness and Robustness of Large Language Models in Reasoning Tasks"
    authors: "Lin et al."
    venue: "ACL 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11005"
    category: evaluation
    role: "First human-annotated SE-AAVE parallel benchmark (ReDial); quantifies LLM performance gaps on AAVE"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "1.2K+ parallel SE-AAVE prompt pairs across reasoning tasks"
      - "Almost all models show statistically significant performance drops on AAVE"
      - "AAVE performance gaps arise from morphosyntactic features and conversational norms"
      - "LLMs struggle more with AAVE than misspelled Standard English"
    how_we_differ: "ReDial evaluates reasoning task performance; we evaluate and calibrate behavioral rates in user simulation"

  - id: faisal2024dialectbench
    title: "DialectBench: A NLP Benchmark for Dialects, Varieties, and Closely-Related Languages"
    authors: "Faisal et al."
    venue: "ACL 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11009"
    category: evaluation
    role: "Large-scale multi-dialect NLP benchmark; documents performance disparities across 281 language varieties"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "10 NLP tasks, 281 varieties, 40 language clusters"
      - "Substantial performance disparities between standard and non-standard varieties"
      - "Performance gap widens with fine-tuning due to uneven data availability"
    how_we_differ: "DialectBench evaluates NLP task performance; we focus on behavioral calibration of user simulators"

  - id: gallegos2024bias
    title: "Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey"
    authors: "Gallegos, Rossi, Barrow et al."
    venue: "Computational Linguistics, Vol. 50(3)"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00770"
    category: evaluation
    role: "Comprehensive survey of LLM bias evaluation and mitigation; provides taxonomy of metrics and datasets"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Taxonomy of bias metrics at embedding, probability, and generated text levels"
      - "Mitigation methods categorized by intervention stage: pre/in/intra/post-processing"
      - "Consolidated public datasets for bias evaluation"
    how_we_differ: "Survey covers general LLM bias; we address a specific bias modality (behavioral rates in user simulation)"

  - id: parrish2022bbq
    title: "BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering"
    authors: "Parrish et al."
    venue: "Findings of ACL 2022"
    year: 2022
    url: "https://aclanthology.org/2022.findings-acl.165/"
    category: evaluation
    role: "Established bias benchmark for QA; evaluates social biases across multiple demographic categories"
    relevance: low
    key_findings:
      - "58,492 unique examples across multiple bias categories"
      - "Evaluates both individual and intersectional biases"
      - "Standard benchmark for LLM bias evaluation"
    how_we_differ: "BBQ measures representational bias in QA; we measure behavioral bias in interactive dialogue simulation"

  - id: haq2026dialect
    title: "Dialect vs Demographics: Quantifying LLM Bias from Implicit Linguistic Signals vs. Explicit User Profiles"
    authors: "Haq, Saldias"
    venue: "arXiv 2604.21152"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21152"
    category: evaluation
    role: "Closest to direct competitor; quantifies how dialect cues vs explicit identity trigger differential LLM behavior"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Dialect cues trigger 'dialect jailbreak' reducing refusal probability to near zero"
      - "AAVE/Singlish users receive less sanitized content than SAE users"
      - "Safety alignment is brittle, over-indexed on explicit keywords"
      - "24,000+ responses analyzed across two LLMs"
    how_we_differ: "They characterize the bias mechanism (implicit vs explicit); we propose calibration methods to correct behavioral rates"

  # BACKGROUND
  # ============================================================
  - id: joshi2025dialect_survey
    title: "Natural Language Processing for Dialects of a Language: A Survey"
    authors: "Joshi, Dabre, Kanojia, Li, Zhan, Haffari, Dippold"
    venue: "ACM Computing Surveys, Vol. 57(6)"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05632"
    category: background
    role: "Comprehensive survey of NLP for dialects; covers datasets, approaches, and performance gaps across dialect varieties"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "NLP models show systematic performance degradation on dialectal data"
      - "Covers NLU and NLG tasks including dialogue systems"
      - "Equity implications of language technology performance gaps"
    how_we_differ: "Survey provides broad context; we tackle a specific gap in user simulation fairness"

  - id: rickford1999aave
    title: "African American Vernacular English: Features, Evolution, Educational Implications"
    authors: "Rickford, John Russell"
    venue: "Blackwell Publishers (Language in Society series)"
    year: 1999
    url: "https://www.amazon.com/African-American-Vernacular-English-Implications/dp/0631212450"
    category: background
    role: "Authoritative reference on AAVE phonological, grammatical, and pragmatic features; grounds our behavioral rate targets"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Systematic documentation of AAVE phonological and grammatical features"
      - "AAVE has distinct pragmatic conventions including directness patterns"
      - "AAVE is a fully systematic linguistic variety, not deficient English"
    how_we_differ: "Provides sociolinguistic grounding for what behavioral patterns we should calibrate toward"

  - id: kachru2008cultures
    title: "Cultures, Contexts, and World Englishes"
    authors: "Kachru, Yamuna; Smith, Cecil"
    venue: "Routledge"
    year: 2008
    url: "https://www.routledge.com/Cultures-Contexts-and-World-Englishes/Kachru-Smith/p/book/9780805847338"
    category: background
    role: "Framework for Indian English pragmatics; documents politeness strategies and speech act differences in Outer Circle Englishes"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Indian English has distinct politeness strategies rooted in face-saving norms"
      - "Requesting and disagreeing strategies differ from Inner Circle varieties"
      - "Three Circles model (Inner/Outer/Expanding) for understanding English variation"
    how_we_differ: "Provides sociolinguistic grounding for Indian English behavioral patterns we calibrate"

  - id: sekulic2024daus
    title: "Reliable LLM-based User Simulator for Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems"
    authors: "Sekulic, Terragni, Guimaraes et al."
    venue: "SCI-CHAT Workshop 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13374"
    category: background
    role: "DAUS: domain-aware user simulator fine-tuned on real dialogues; shows fine-tuning improves goal fulfillment and reduces hallucination"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Fine-tuning LLMs on real dialogue examples improves user goal fulfillment"
      - "Mitigates hallucinations in simulator responses"
      - "Domain-aware approach outperforms generic prompting"
    how_we_differ: "DAUS optimizes task completion; we optimize demographic behavioral fidelity"

  - id: ahmad2025diversity
    title: "Simulating User Diversity in Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems using Large Language Models"
    authors: "Ahmad, Hillmann, Moller"
    venue: "arXiv 2502.12813"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12813"
    category: background
    role: "Generates diverse user profiles with varied demographics and conversational styles for dialogue evaluation"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "GPT-o1 generates more heterogeneous user distributions than GPT-4o"
      - "82.46% task success across 57 dialogue sessions with diverse users"
      - "Captures variation in language styles, knowledge levels, and objectives"
    how_we_differ: "They generate diverse profiles; we calibrate specific behavioral rates to match real dialect group distributions"

  - id: sim2real2026gap
    title: "Mind the Sim2Real Gap in User Simulation for Agentic Tasks"
    authors: "Zhou, Sun, Xu, Chen, Radev"
    venue: "arXiv 2603.11245"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11245"
    category: foundation
    role: "First study running full τ-bench protocol with 451 real humans; introduces USI metric to quantify sim-vs-human behavioral divergence"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "LLM simulators are excessively cooperative, stylistically uniform, and lack realistic frustration/ambiguity"
      - "Simulated users create 'easy mode' that inflates agent success rates above human baseline"
      - "Simulated feedback is uniformly positive; humans express calibrated dissatisfaction"
      - "Higher model capability does not yield more faithful user simulation"
    how_we_differ: "They quantify the sim2real gap but do not propose calibration methods; we use DPO to close the behavioral rate gap for specific dialect groups"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"
    note: "Near-competitor in problem framing — directly validates our motivation. Not a direct competitor because they diagnose without prescribing a fix."

  # --- METHOD-COMPONENT (new) ---
  - id: khan2026decoding
    title: "Decoding-Time Debiasing via Process Reward Models: From Controlled Fill-in to Open-Ended Generation"
    authors: "Khan, Muneeb Ur Raheem"
    venue: "arXiv 2605.02348"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02348"
    category: method-component
    role: "Decoding-time bias mitigation using Process Reward Model as fairness judge; alternative to our training-time DPO approach"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Sequential debiasing raises bias scores by up to +0.40 over baseline while preserving fluency"
      - "No weight changes needed — debiasing happens at inference via PRM scoring"
      - "Gate calibration is model-dependent; no one-size-fits-all prompt works"
    how_we_differ: "They debias at decoding time for general fairness; we train the simulator via DPO to match target behavioral distributions"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"

  # --- EVALUATION (new) ---
  - id: gupta2025endive
    title: "EnDive: A Cross-Dialect Benchmark for Fairness and Performance in Large Language Models"
    authors: "Gupta, Cheung et al."
    venue: "Findings of EMNLP 2025 (arXiv 2504.07100)"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07100"
    category: evaluation
    role: "Cross-dialect benchmark covering 5 dialects including AAVE and Indian English — both our target dialects"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Covers AAVE (33M speakers), Indian English (250M speakers), Jamaican, Chicano, Singaporean English"
      - "Few-shot LLM translation of SE to dialects, validated by native speakers (avg 6.02/7 faithfulness)"
      - "LLMs show performance drops on non-standard dialects across understanding, reasoning, math, logic"
    how_we_differ: "EnDive evaluates NLP task performance across dialects; we calibrate user simulator behavioral rates for those same dialect groups"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"

  # --- METHOD-COMPONENT (new, Plan B relevant) ---
  - id: lee2024dpo_toxicity
    title: "A Mechanistic Understanding of Alignment Algorithms: A Case Study on DPO and Toxicity"
    authors: "Lee, Panda, Yun, Bansal"
    venue: "ICML 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01967"
    category: method-component
    role: "Shows DPO bypasses rather than removes pre-training capabilities; explains mechanistically why DPO+BCP can reverse calibration direction"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "DPO does not remove toxic capabilities, only bypasses them at inference"
      - "Simple un-alignment can revert model to pre-DPO behavior"
      - "Minimal parameter changes allow reversion — alignment is fragile"
    how_we_differ: "They study DPO toxicity mechanics; we document DPO+BCP calibration reversal as a specific failure mode"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"
    plan_b_relevance: "FM4 — explains why DPO training can reverse BCP calibration effect"

  - id: gupta2026intra_fairness
    title: "Intra-Fairness Dynamics: The Bias Spillover Effect in Targeted LLM Alignment"
    authors: "Paraschou, Heiter, Iosifidis"
    venue: "arXiv 2602.16438"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16438"
    category: method-component
    role: "Documents bias spillover — targeted debiasing on one dimension causes unintended effects on other dimensions; directly parallels our cross-dimension interference"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Targeted debiasing can produce unintended negative consequences across other social axes"
      - "Bias spillover effect: altering behavior on one dimension when mitigating another"
      - "Multi-attribute fairness dynamics must be considered in alignment"
    how_we_differ: "They study bias spillover in general alignment; we document the specific cross-dimension interference pattern in BCP-based behavioral calibration"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"
    plan_b_relevance: "FM2 + FM4 — directly supports cross-dimension interference and DPO spillover claims"

  - id: basil2025playing_pretend
    title: "Prompting Science Report 4: Playing Pretend: Expert Personas Don't Improve Factual Accuracy"
    authors: "Basil, Shapiro, Shapiro, Mollick, Mollick, Meincke"
    venue: "arXiv 2512.05858 (Wharton)"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05858"
    category: method-component
    role: "Shows persona prompting degrades factual accuracy; BCP is a form of persona/role prompting, explaining completion collapse"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Expert personas do not improve factual accuracy across benchmarks"
      - "Persona prompting activates instruction-following mode at expense of factual recall"
      - "MMLU accuracy drops from 71.6% baseline to 66.3% with detailed persona"
    how_we_differ: "They study persona prompting in classification/QA; we document the same mechanism in multi-turn dialogue task completion"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"
    plan_b_relevance: "FM1 — explains mechanism behind global behavior suppression"

  - id: hu2026expert_persona
    title: "Expert Personas Improve LLM Alignment but Damage Accuracy: Bootstrapping Intent-Based Persona Routing with PRISM"
    authors: "Hu, Rostami, Thomason"
    venue: "arXiv 2603.18507"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18507"
    category: method-component
    role: "Systematically documents persona prompting trade-off: alignment improves but accuracy degrades up to 30pp; directly explains BCP completion collapse"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Persona prompting improves alignment tasks but degrades knowledge/reasoning tasks"
      - "Performance drops up to 30pp under persona modifications"
      - "More instruction-tuned models are more susceptible to persona-induced accuracy loss"
    how_we_differ: "They study general persona-accuracy trade-off; we document the specific completion collapse in agent-user dialogue under behavioral calibration prompts"
    scan_date: "2026-05-13"
    plan_b_relevance: "FM1 — strongest external evidence for global behavior suppression mechanism"

  # ============================================================
  # DIRECT-COMPETITOR
  # ============================================================
  # 未找到直接竞品。没有现有工作专门做"校准 LLM 用户模拟器的方言行为率偏差"。
  # 最接近的是 Haq & Saldias 2026（归入 evaluation），但他们只量化偏差，不提出校准方法。
  # 这验证了 DemoCalib 的新颖性。

  # ============================================================
  # FOUNDATION
  # ============================================================
  - id: seshadri2026lost
    title: "Lost in Simulation: LLM-Simulated Users are Unreliable Proxies for Human Users in Agentic Evaluations"
    authors: "Seshadri, Cahyawijaya, Odumakinde, Singh, Goldfarb-Tarrant"
    venue: "arXiv 2601.17087"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17087"
    category: foundation
    role: "Documents that LLM user simulators are differentially effective proxies across demographic groups; AAVE and Indian English speakers get worst calibration"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Agent success rates vary up to 9pp across different user simulator LLMs"
      - "AAVE speakers experience consistently worse success rates and calibration errors than SAE speakers"
      - "Simulated users introduce conversational artifacts absent from real human users"
      - "Disparities compound significantly with age for AAVE speakers"
    how_we_differ: "They document the problem; we document why both BCP and DPO calibration fail to close the gaps, providing a failure taxonomy"

  - id: yao2024taubench
    title: "tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains"
    authors: "Yao et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2406.12045"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045"
    category: foundation
    role: "The agent evaluation framework we build on; provides retail customer service domain with user simulator + tool-calling agent + pass^k metric"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Even gpt-4o succeeds on <50% of tasks; pass^8 <25% in retail"
      - "Proposes pass^k metric measuring reliability over multiple trials"
      - "User simulator is LLM-based, enabling behavioral modification"
    how_we_differ: "We extend tau-bench by documenting systematic failure modes when calibrating the user simulator's dialect-specific behavioral rates"

  - id: liu2024agentbench
    title: "AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents"
    authors: "Liu et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.03688"
    category: foundation
    role: "Multi-environment agent benchmark; establishes evaluation methodology for LLM agents across 8 environments"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Significant performance gap between commercial and open-source LLMs as agents"
      - "Poor long-term reasoning and instruction following are main obstacles"
    how_we_differ: "AgentBench evaluates agent capability; we focus on user simulator fidelity and fairness"

  - id: wang2024mint
    title: "MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback"
    authors: "Wang, Wang, Liu, Chen, Yuan, Peng, Ji"
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10691"
    category: foundation
    role: "Multi-turn agent evaluation benchmark; shows gap between single-turn and multi-turn performance"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "LLMs benefit 1-8% per turn from tools, 2-17% from language feedback"
      - "Better single-turn performance does not guarantee better multi-turn performance"
      - "SIFT and RLHF generally hurt multi-turn capabilities"
    how_we_differ: "MINT uses GPT-4 simulated users without demographic variation; we investigate dialect-aware calibration and document its failure modes"

  # ============================================================
  # METHOD-COMPONENT
  # ============================================================
  - id: rafailov2023dpo
    title: "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model"
    authors: "Rafailov, Sharma, Mitchell, Manning, Ermon, Finn"
    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290"
    category: method-component
    role: "Core algorithm for our DPO-based behavioral alignment; eliminates need for reward model training"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "DPO directly optimizes policy from preference pairs without explicit reward model"
      - "Computationally lightweight, stable alternative to PPO-based RLHF"
      - "Exceeds PPO-based RLHF in controlling sentiment of generations"
    how_we_differ: "We apply DPO to attempt dialect behavioral calibration and document its systematic failure modes including calibration reversal"

  - id: zhao2021calibrate
    title: "Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models"
    authors: "Zhao, Wallace, Feng, Klein, Singh"
    venue: "ICML 2021"
    year: 2021
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09690"
    category: method-component
    role: "Foundational calibration method for LLMs; contextual calibration corrects output distribution biases"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Few-shot accuracy varies from near chance to near SOTA depending on prompt format"
      - "Identified majority label bias, recency bias, common token bias"
      - "Contextual calibration with content-free inputs improves accuracy up to 30%"
    how_we_differ: "They calibrate classification outputs; we attempt to calibrate behavioral rates (question rate, politeness) in generation and document why it fails"

  - id: abdulhai2025consistent
    title: "Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "Abdulhai, Cheng, Clay, Althoff, Levine, Jaques"
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00222"
    category: method-component
    role: "Multi-turn RL for persona consistency; directly relevant to maintaining calibrated behavior across conversation turns"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Off-the-shelf LLMs drift from assigned personas over multi-turn dialogue"
      - "Three automatic metrics: prompt-to-line, line-to-line, Q&A consistency"
      - "Multi-turn RL reduces inconsistency by >55%"
    how_we_differ: "They optimize persona consistency in general; we document failure modes when targeting dialect behavioral rate calibration"

  - id: naous2025flipping
    title: "Flipping the Dialogue: Training and Evaluating User Language Models"
    authors: "Naous, Laban, Xu, Neville"
    venue: "arXiv 2510.06552"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06552"
    category: method-component
    role: "Purpose-built User LMs outperform repurposed assistant LMs as user simulators; validates need for specialized user models"
    relevance: high
    key_findings:
      - "Better assistant LMs yield worse user simulators"
      - "UserLM-8b provides more realistic user simulation"
      - "GPT-4o performance drops from 74.6% to 57.4% under realistic user simulation"
    how_we_differ: "They train general User LMs; we document why calibrating user simulator behavioral rates for specific dialect groups fails"

  - id: li2025persona
    title: "LLM Generated Persona is a Promise with a Catch"
    authors: "Li, Chen et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16527"
    category: method-component
    role: "Documents systematic biases in LLM-generated personas; explains why naive persona prompting fails for demographic simulation"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "LLM-generated personas systematically drift toward socially desirable traits"
      - "More LLM-generated content produces more left-leaning, less representative personas"
      - "Bias exists in the persona creation step itself, not just model responses"
    how_we_differ: "We document failure modes when directly injecting behavioral rate targets via BCP, including persona-like completion collapse"

  - id: wang2024alignment
    title: "A Comprehensive Survey of LLM Alignment Techniques: RLHF, RLAIF, PPO, DPO and More"
    authors: "Wang, Bi, Pentyala et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2407.16216"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16216"
    category: method-component
    role: "Survey unifying alignment methods under single policy gradient framework; reference for our DPO methodology"
    relevance: medium
    key_findings:
      - "Unified policy gradient framework for pretraining, SFT, RLHF, RLVR"
      - "DPO is stable and lightweight but sensitive to preference data quality"
      - "Detailed comparison of PPO vs GRPO vs DPO implementation details"
    how_we_differ: "Survey provides methodology reference; we apply DPO to user simulator dialect calibration and document its failure modes"

1	# Paper Framing: Calibration Failure Taxonomy for LLM User Simulators
2	
3	> Plan B story — Director approved 2026-05-13
4	> Target: EMNLP 2026 Findings (ARR deadline 2026-05-25)
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Title Candidates
9	
10	1. **"Why Calibration Fails: A Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Dialect-Aware LLM User Simulation"**
11	   - Pro: 直接点明贡献（taxonomy），关键词覆盖好
12	   - Con: 稍长
13	
14	2. **"The Calibration Trap: Prompt-Based and Training-Based Corrections Both Fail for Dialect Bias in LLM User Simulators"**
15	   - Pro: "trap" 吸引眼球，涵盖两种方法
16	   - Con: 可能暗示过于 negative
17	
18	3. **"Behavioral Calibration Considered Harmful? Systematic Failure Modes in Dialect-Aware User Simulation"**
19	   - Pro: Dijkstra 风格标题引发好奇，问号留余地
20	   - Con: "Considered Harmful" 可能被认为 cliché
21	
22	**推荐**: Title 1 — 最准确传达贡献，reviewer-friendly。
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Core Story
27	
28	**Problem**: LLM user simulators exhibit dialect-dependent behavioral biases — AAVE and Indian English speakers receive systematically different politeness and question-asking patterns compared to Standard American English (sim2real2026gap; seshadri2026lost). These biases propagate into agent evaluation, undermining fairness.
29	
30	**Attempted Solution**: We apply two complementary calibration strategies:
31	- **BCP (Behavioral Calibration Prompting)**: Prompt-level injection of target behavioral rates
32	- **DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)**: Training-level alignment using dialect-calibrated preference pairs
33	
34	**Finding**: Both strategies fail systematically. We document **the first taxonomy of calibration failure modes** for LLM user simulators, identifying four distinct mechanisms that explain why seemingly reasonable calibration interventions produce counterproductive outcomes.
35	
36	**Framing**: This is NOT "we tried and failed." This is a systematic empirical analysis that (1) identifies previously undocumented failure mechanisms, (2) connects them to known phenomena in persona prompting and alignment, and (3) provides actionable constraints for future calibration research.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Core Claims
41	
42	### C1: BCP produces three systematic failure mechanisms
43	**Evidence strength**: Moderate (single model, single run, n=19-20 per variant)
44	
45	| Failure Mode | Description | Key Metric | exp_id |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| FM1: Global Behavior Suppression | BCP calibration prompts collapse task completion regardless of target dimension | completion retention 52.3% (threshold ≥80%) | mvp-004 |
48	| FM2: Cross-Dimension Interference | Targeting one behavioral dimension perturbs non-targeted dimensions | politeness -25.6% when targeting question_rate; question_rate -52.3% when targeting politeness | mvp-004 |
49	| FM3: Overcorrection Rebound | Requesting extreme behavioral shift causes model to rebound in opposite direction | overcorrected politeness +4.2pp ~ +10.4pp above baseline (4 runs, 4/4 consistent) | hgate-dpo003-merged |
50	
51	**Supporting numbers (mvp-004, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, n=19-20)**:
52	- FM1: aave completion 0.100 vs baseline 0.368 (-72.8%); indian 0.150 (-59.2%); mean calibrated 0.193
53	- FM2: single_dim_question politeness drops 25.6% (non-target); single_dim_politeness question_rate drops 52.3% (non-target)
54	  - **Base rate caveat**: question_rate baseline = 0.044 (~0.8 questions/task); 52.3% drop = absolute change from ~0.044 to ~0.021. Paper must report both absolute values and relative changes.
55	- FM3: **[primary]** hgate-dpo003-merged overcorrected politeness mean 0.574 vs baseline 0.502, gap +7.2pp (+14.3% relative), range +4.2pp ~ +10.4pp, 4/4 runs consistent; **[auxiliary]** mvp-004 single run: 0.605 vs 0.559 (+4.6pp, +8.2% relative)
56	
57	**External support**:
58	- FM1: basil2025playing_pretend (persona prompting drops MMLU 71.6%→66.3%); hu2026expert_persona (accuracy degradation up to 30pp under persona)
59	- FM2: gupta2026intra_fairness (bias spillover effect in targeted alignment)
60	- FM3: no direct external parallel — novel observation
61	
62	### C2: DPO+BCP interaction produces calibration reversal
63	**Evidence strength**: Strong (single model, 4 runs × 20 tasks = 80 episodes)
64	
65	DPO training, despite learning effectively (acc 0.75-1.0, loss 0.653), reverses BCP calibration direction when combined:
66	
67	| Metric | Base BCP (mvp-004) | DPO+BCP (hgate-dpo003-merged) |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| AAVE politeness gap | -0.091 (correct direction) | +0.064 (**reversed**) |
70	| Indian politeness gap | -0.099 (correct direction) | +0.063 (**reversed**) |
71	| H2 gap reduction | 25-28% (close to 30% threshold) | **-10.3%** (wrong direction) |
72	| Variant×run checks with gap expansion | — | **10/12** |
73	| Overcorrection rebound | +8.2% | **+14.3%** (amplified) |
74	
75	**Key insight**: DPO-003 training *improved* tool-calling ability (merged completion 60% vs base 40%, diag-lora-merge). The reversal is not a DPO training failure — it's an **interaction effect** between DPO alignment and BCP prompting.
76	
77	**External support**: lee2024dpo_toxicity (DPO bypasses rather than removes capabilities; alignment is fragile and reversible)
78	
79	### C3: Cross-scale validation
80	**Evidence strength**: [PENDING: qwen14b-bcp-001]
81	
82	Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ BCP evaluation in progress. If FM1-FM3 replicate at 14B scale, this strengthens the claim that failure modes are structural (not capacity-limited).
83	
84	**Current auxiliary evidence**:
85	- Llama-3-8B (llama-bcp-001): Floor effect (completion=5%). Only supports "behavior shift observable at floor completion." **Cannot claim cross-model generalization** — tool-calling too weak to isolate BCP effect.
86	- Mistral-7B (mistral-bcp-001): completion=0%, model cannot do structured tool_calls with 16 tools. No usable data.
87	
88	**Hedging strategy**: If Qwen14B replicates → "failure modes persist across model scales (7B, 14B)." If not → limit scope to "documented on Qwen2.5-7B; generalizability requires further investigation."
89	
90	### C4: Implications for future calibration research
91	**Evidence strength**: Analytical (grounded in C1-C3)
92	
93	- **Implication 1**: Prompt-based calibration of behavioral rates in multi-turn agent dialogue is fundamentally limited by the completion-calibration trade-off (FM1). This parallels the persona-accuracy trade-off (basil2025playing_pretend; hu2026expert_persona) but is more severe in agentic settings where tool-calling capability is at stake.
94	- **Implication 2**: Behavioral dimensions are coupled — calibrating politeness rate without affecting question rate (or completion) requires methods that can disentangle dimensions (FM2). Possible direction: per-dimension reward models or constrained decoding (cf. khan2026decoding).
95	- **Implication 3**: DPO alignment and prompt-based calibration can interact adversarially (FM4). Future work must evaluate calibration methods in combination, not in isolation.
96	- **Implication 4**: Overcorrection rebound (FM3) suggests models have an "attractor basin" for default behavioral rates that resists large perturbations. Gradual/iterative calibration may outperform one-shot extreme targets.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Reviewer Concerns (Pre-empted Attack Surfaces)
101	
102	### RC1: "Single model — how do we know this generalizes?"
103	**Status**: Partially mitigated
104	- Qwen14B data [PENDING: qwen14b-bcp-001] provides cross-scale evidence
105	- Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B failed due to tool-calling limitations, NOT because BCP worked on them
106	- FM1 aligns with persona-accuracy trade-off documented across GPT-4, Claude, Llama in basil2025playing_pretend and hu2026expert_persona
107	- **Honest hedge**: "We document these failure modes on Qwen2.5-7B; external evidence from persona prompting literature suggests the mechanisms are general, but direct multi-model verification for agent dialogue remains future work."
108	
109	### RC2: "n=20 tasks, high variance — statistical power?"
110	**Response**:
111	- BCP results (mvp-004): n=19-20 per variant, single run. Variance is a valid concern for absolute numbers.
112	- DPO+BCP results (hgate-dpo003-merged): 4 independent runs × 20 tasks = 80 episodes. Reversal effect consistent across 10/12 variant×run checks — this is not a variance artifact.
113	- FM3 (rebound): consistent direction in 4/4 runs for overcorrected variant.
114	- **Mitigation**: Report all individual run data (no cherry-picking, per memory.md rule). Frame claims around direction and consistency, not precise magnitudes.
115	
116	### RC3: "This is just negative results — where's the contribution?"
117	**Response**:
118	- Negative-results papers exist at top venues (e.g., Findings track). But this is MORE than negative results:
119	  1. **Taxonomy**: First systematic categorization of calibration failure modes (FM1-FM4)
120	  2. **Mechanistic connections**: Link FM1→persona-accuracy trade-off, FM2→bias spillover, FM4→DPO bypass
121	  3. **Actionable implications**: Concrete constraints for future calibration methods
122	  4. **Interaction discovery**: FM4 (DPO+BCP reversal) is novel — no prior work documents this interaction
123	
124	### RC4: "Why not try other calibration methods?"
125	**Response**:
126	- BCP and DPO represent the two main paradigms (prompt-time vs training-time). Covering both provides good coverage.
127	- Paper scope is diagnosis (failure taxonomy), not exhaustive method search.
128	- Implications section points to alternative approaches (constrained decoding, per-dimension reward, iterative calibration).
129	
130	### RC5: "The evaluation framework (tau-bench) is a confound — maybe BCP works on simpler tasks?"
131	**Response**:
132	- tau-bench is the standard benchmark for tool-calling agent evaluation (yao2024taubench; sim2real2026gap uses it too).
133	- FM1 parallels persona-accuracy trade-off found on MMLU/general benchmarks — not tau-bench specific.
134	- But fairly: FM2 and FM3 may be task-dependent. Acknowledged in limitations.
135

153	
154	## Contribution Statement
155	
156	We present the first systematic taxonomy of calibration failure modes for LLM user simulators in agentic evaluation. Through controlled experiments on Qwen2.5-7B in the tau-bench retail domain, we identify four failure mechanisms — global behavior suppression, cross-dimension interference, overcorrection rebound, and DPO-BCP interaction reversal — that explain why both prompt-based and training-based calibration methods fail to correct dialect-dependent behavioral biases. Our findings establish concrete constraints for future calibration research and connect observed failures to broader phenomena in persona prompting and preference optimization.
157	
158	---

# Paper Framing: Calibration Failure Taxonomy for LLM User Simulators

> Plan B story — Director approved 2026-05-13
> Target: EMNLP 2026 Findings (ARR deadline 2026-05-25)

---

## Title Candidates

1. **"Why Calibration Fails: A Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Dialect-Aware LLM User Simulation"**
   - Pro: 直接点明贡献（taxonomy），关键词覆盖好
   - Con: 稍长

2. **"The Calibration Trap: Prompt-Based and Training-Based Corrections Both Fail for Dialect Bias in LLM User Simulators"**
   - Pro: "trap" 吸引眼球，涵盖两种方法
   - Con: 可能暗示过于 negative

3. **"Behavioral Calibration Considered Harmful? Systematic Failure Modes in Dialect-Aware User Simulation"**
   - Pro: Dijkstra 风格标题引发好奇，问号留余地
   - Con: "Considered Harmful" 可能被认为 cliché

**推荐**: Title 1 — 最准确传达贡献，reviewer-friendly。

---

## Core Story

**Problem**: LLM user simulators exhibit dialect-dependent behavioral biases — AAVE and Indian English speakers receive systematically different politeness and question-asking patterns compared to Standard American English (sim2real2026gap; seshadri2026lost). These biases propagate into agent evaluation, undermining fairness.

**Attempted Solution**: We apply two complementary calibration strategies:
- **BCP (Behavioral Calibration Prompting)**: Prompt-level injection of target behavioral rates
- **DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)**: Training-level alignment using dialect-calibrated preference pairs

**Finding**: Both strategies fail systematically. We document **the first taxonomy of calibration failure modes** for LLM user simulators, identifying four distinct mechanisms that explain why seemingly reasonable calibration interventions produce counterproductive outcomes.

**Framing**: This is NOT "we tried and failed." This is a systematic empirical analysis that (1) identifies previously undocumented failure mechanisms, (2) connects them to known phenomena in persona prompting and alignment, and (3) provides actionable constraints for future calibration research.

---

## Core Claims

### C1: BCP produces three systematic failure mechanisms
**Evidence strength**: Moderate (single model, single run, n=19-20 per variant)

| Failure Mode | Description | Key Metric | exp_id |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM1: Global Behavior Suppression | BCP calibration prompts collapse task completion regardless of target dimension | completion retention 52.3% (threshold ≥80%) | mvp-004 |
| FM2: Cross-Dimension Interference | Targeting one behavioral dimension perturbs non-targeted dimensions | politeness -25.6% when targeting question_rate; question_rate -52.3% when targeting politeness | mvp-004 |
| FM3: Overcorrection Rebound | Requesting extreme behavioral shift causes model to rebound in opposite direction | overcorrected politeness +4.2pp ~ +10.4pp above baseline (4 runs, 4/4 consistent) | hgate-dpo003-merged |

**Supporting numbers (mvp-004, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, n=19-20)**:
- FM1: aave completion 0.100 vs baseline 0.368 (-72.8%); indian 0.150 (-59.2%); mean calibrated 0.193
- FM2: single_dim_question politeness drops 25.6% (non-target); single_dim_politeness question_rate drops 52.3% (non-target)
  - **Base rate caveat**: question_rate baseline = 0.044 (~0.8 questions/task); 52.3% drop = absolute change from ~0.044 to ~0.021. Paper must report both absolute values and relative changes.
- FM3: **[primary]** hgate-dpo003-merged overcorrected politeness mean 0.574 vs baseline 0.502, gap +7.2pp (+14.3% relative), range +4.2pp ~ +10.4pp, 4/4 runs consistent; **[auxiliary]** mvp-004 single run: 0.605 vs 0.559 (+4.6pp, +8.2% relative)

**External support**:
- FM1: basil2025playing_pretend (persona prompting drops MMLU 71.6%→66.3%); hu2026expert_persona (accuracy degradation up to 30pp under persona)
- FM2: gupta2026intra_fairness (bias spillover effect in targeted alignment)
- FM3: no direct external parallel — novel observation

### C2: DPO+BCP interaction produces calibration reversal
**Evidence strength**: Strong (single model, 4 runs × 20 tasks = 80 episodes)

DPO training, despite learning effectively (acc 0.75-1.0, loss 0.653), reverses BCP calibration direction when combined:

| Metric | Base BCP (mvp-004) | DPO+BCP (hgate-dpo003-merged) |
|---|---|---|
| AAVE politeness gap | -0.091 (correct direction) | +0.064 (**reversed**) |
| Indian politeness gap | -0.099 (correct direction) | +0.063 (**reversed**) |
| H2 gap reduction | 25-28% (close to 30% threshold) | **-10.3%** (wrong direction) |
| Variant×run checks with gap expansion | — | **10/12** |
| Overcorrection rebound | +8.2% | **+14.3%** (amplified) |

**Key insight**: DPO-003 training *improved* tool-calling ability (merged completion 60% vs base 40%, diag-lora-merge). The reversal is not a DPO training failure — it's an **interaction effect** between DPO alignment and BCP prompting.

**External support**: lee2024dpo_toxicity (DPO bypasses rather than removes capabilities; alignment is fragile and reversible)

### C3: Cross-scale validation
**Evidence strength**: [PENDING: qwen14b-bcp-001]

Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ BCP evaluation in progress. If FM1-FM3 replicate at 14B scale, this strengthens the claim that failure modes are structural (not capacity-limited).

**Current auxiliary evidence**:
- Llama-3-8B (llama-bcp-001): Floor effect (completion=5%). Only supports "behavior shift observable at floor completion." **Cannot claim cross-model generalization** — tool-calling too weak to isolate BCP effect.
- Mistral-7B (mistral-bcp-001): completion=0%, model cannot do structured tool_calls with 16 tools. No usable data.

**Hedging strategy**: If Qwen14B replicates → "failure modes persist across model scales (7B, 14B)." If not → limit scope to "documented on Qwen2.5-7B; generalizability requires further investigation."

### C4: Implications for future calibration research
**Evidence strength**: Analytical (grounded in C1-C3)

- **Implication 1**: Prompt-based calibration of behavioral rates in multi-turn agent dialogue is fundamentally limited by the completion-calibration trade-off (FM1). This parallels the persona-accuracy trade-off (basil2025playing_pretend; hu2026expert_persona) but is more severe in agentic settings where tool-calling capability is at stake.
- **Implication 2**: Behavioral dimensions are coupled — calibrating politeness rate without affecting question rate (or completion) requires methods that can disentangle dimensions (FM2). Possible direction: per-dimension reward models or constrained decoding (cf. khan2026decoding).
- **Implication 3**: DPO alignment and prompt-based calibration can interact adversarially (FM4). Future work must evaluate calibration methods in combination, not in isolation.
- **Implication 4**: Overcorrection rebound (FM3) suggests models have an "attractor basin" for default behavioral rates that resists large perturbations. Gradual/iterative calibration may outperform one-shot extreme targets.

---

## Reviewer Concerns (Pre-empted Attack Surfaces)

### RC1: "Single model — how do we know this generalizes?"
**Status**: Partially mitigated
- Qwen14B data [PENDING: qwen14b-bcp-001] provides cross-scale evidence
- Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B failed due to tool-calling limitations, NOT because BCP worked on them
- FM1 aligns with persona-accuracy trade-off documented across GPT-4, Claude, Llama in basil2025playing_pretend and hu2026expert_persona
- **Honest hedge**: "We document these failure modes on Qwen2.5-7B; external evidence from persona prompting literature suggests the mechanisms are general, but direct multi-model verification for agent dialogue remains future work."

### RC2: "n=20 tasks, high variance — statistical power?"
**Response**:
- BCP results (mvp-004): n=19-20 per variant, single run. Variance is a valid concern for absolute numbers.
- DPO+BCP results (hgate-dpo003-merged): 4 independent runs × 20 tasks = 80 episodes. Reversal effect consistent across 10/12 variant×run checks — this is not a variance artifact.
- FM3 (rebound): consistent direction in 4/4 runs for overcorrected variant.
- **Mitigation**: Report all individual run data (no cherry-picking, per memory.md rule). Frame claims around direction and consistency, not precise magnitudes.

### RC3: "This is just negative results — where's the contribution?"
**Response**:
- Negative-results papers exist at top venues (e.g., Findings track). But this is MORE than negative results:
  1. **Taxonomy**: First systematic categorization of calibration failure modes (FM1-FM4)
  2. **Mechanistic connections**: Link FM1→persona-accuracy trade-off, FM2→bias spillover, FM4→DPO bypass
  3. **Actionable implications**: Concrete constraints for future calibration methods
  4. **Interaction discovery**: FM4 (DPO+BCP reversal) is novel — no prior work documents this interaction

### RC4: "Why not try other calibration methods?"
**Response**:
- BCP and DPO represent the two main paradigms (prompt-time vs training-time). Covering both provides good coverage.
- Paper scope is diagnosis (failure taxonomy), not exhaustive method search.
- Implications section points to alternative approaches (constrained decoding, per-dimension reward, iterative calibration).

### RC5: "The evaluation framework (tau-bench) is a confound — maybe BCP works on simpler tasks?"
**Response**:
- tau-bench is the standard benchmark for tool-calling agent evaluation (yao2024taubench; sim2real2026gap uses it too).
- FM1 parallels persona-accuracy trade-off found on MMLU/general benchmarks — not tau-bench specific.
- But fairly: FM2 and FM3 may be task-dependent. Acknowledged in limitations.

---

## Evidence Map

| Claim | Sub-claim | Primary Experiment | Metric | Value | Secondary Experiment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | FM1: completion collapse | mvp-004 | mean completion retention | 52.3% (need ≥80%) | hgate-dpo003-merged (excl. run2: 47-51% drop) |
| C1 | FM2: cross-dim interference | mvp-004 | non-target dim shift | politeness -25.6%, qrate -52.3% | — |
| C1 | FM3: overcorrection rebound | hgate-dpo003-merged | overcorrected pol vs baseline | +7.2pp mean (+14.3% rel), 4/4 runs consistent | mvp-004 (+4.6pp, single run) |
| C2 | FM4: DPO reversal of BCP | hgate-dpo003-merged | H2 gap reduction | -10.3% (wrong direction) | — |
| C2 | FM4: gap expansion count | hgate-dpo003-merged | variant×run checks | 10/12 expanded | — |
| C2 | DPO training effective | dpo-003 | rewards accuracy | 0.75-1.0 | diag-lora-merge (merged 60% vs base 40%) |
| C2 | Direction comparison | mvp-004 vs hgate-dpo003-merged | AAVE pol gap | -0.091 → +0.064 | Indian: -0.099 → +0.063 |
| C3 | Cross-scale (7B→14B) | [PENDING: qwen14b-bcp-001] | FM1-FM3 replication | [PENDING] | — |
| C3 | Cross-model (auxiliary) | llama-bcp-001 | completion | 5% (floor) | Not usable for generalization |

---

| FM4 mechanism | lee2024dpo_toxicity (ICML 2024) | DPO bypasses rather than removes capabilities; fragile alignment |
| Evaluation framework | yao2024taubench (arXiv 2406.12045) | τ-bench retail domain, pass^k metric |
| Bias context | seshadri2026lost (arXiv 2601.17087) | AAVE/Indian English speakers get worst simulator calibration |
| DPO method | rafailov2023dpo (NeurIPS 2023) | Core DPO algorithm reference |

---
